title: ATM Hardware Cash Dispenser & Bounded Knapsack Allocation
subtitle: Physical Paper Jam Compensation, Dynamic Programming Dispense & 2-Phase Ledger Hold
problem_statement: Designing the cash dispensing subsystem of an Automated Teller Machine (ATM) with physical bill cassettes (5000₽, 2000₽, 1000₽, 500₽, 200₽, 100₽). Greedy allocation fails on denominations (e.g. dispensing 600₽ from 500₽ and 200₽ bills requires Bounded Knapsack), physical actuator motor has high mechanical latency and cannot be pulsed incrementally, and mechanical paper jams require automated ledger compensation.

faded_bug.description: Greedy bill selection fails when smaller combinations can fulfill the request, and lack of 2-phase hold/clear leads to double-spending or money loss during paper jams.

invariants.description: Customer account balance must be debited ONLY for the bills physically passed through the optical exit sensor.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Why does a greedy banknote dispensing algorithm fail for an ATM? Give a concrete counter-example with Russian ruble denominations.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If the physical motor jams halfway through dispensing, how does the firmware know how many banknotes were actually dispensed before the jam?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: Suppose power is cut to the ATM after the bill shutter opens but before the network confirmation packet reaches the core ledger. How does reconciliation work?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: How do you optimize the Bounded Knapsack algorithm so it computes bill distribution in < 2ms on an embedded Intel Atom / ARM CPU inside the ATM?

counter_probes.counter_question: If you have 500₽ and 200₽ bills and the user requests 600₽, what does greedy output? How do you fix this?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Greedy picks 500₽, leaves 100₽, and fails because there are no 100₽ bills left. Dynamic programming (Bounded Knapsack) or backtracking finds the 3x200₽ solution.
